region: Närke, on the plain south of Örebro
description: Ten years ago Kärrtorp was a parish of farms on the flat Närke plain; then the western main line came through, a junction was built where the branch to Örebro meets it, and a town of railway workers, merchants and hotels has grown up around the station. New wooden houses stand on lots between old farms, and the church bell competes with the station bell. The farmers grumble about the smoke and the newcomers but sell them milk and hay.
seasonNotes: November, the darkest and dreariest month. Low clouds lie over the plain, it rains or sleets most days, and the roads are rivers of mud. It is dark by half past three, and paraffin lamps burn around the station from mid-afternoon. Locomotives' smoke hangs in the wet air. Farmers are threshing and slaughtering; Martinmas brings goose dinners and the end of the servants' year, when hired hands change places.
travel: From Uppsala by rail to Stockholm (about 2 hours), change stations, by the trunk line to Katrineholm (about 3 hours) and by the western main line to Kärrtorp Junction (about 2 hours): some seven hours on the rails and eight with the change, all year; the slow alternative is the post road via Enköping, Västerås and Arboga, two days.

geography.realAnalogue: Hallsberg (the Närke plain south of Örebro, where the western main line meets the Örebro branch)
knownFor: A new railway junction where the western main line meets the branch to Örebro, and a town of railway hands and hotels that has grown up in ten years
The flat Närke plain of old freehold farms, with the great marsh east of the town that floods every autumn
Its closeness to Örebro, with its castle and county administration, and to Lake Hjälmaren and its old canal to the Mälaren

neighbours.name: Hallsberg
neighbours.kind: railway town and crown sheriff's seat
neighbours.distance: about 12 km along the main line, a short train ride or half a day by cart on the autumn roads

neighbours.name: Örebro
neighbours.distance: about 35 km north by the branch line, roughly an hour by train
offers: Governor and county administration in the castle
Örebro Privatbank and a savings bank
Large market and shops, booksellers and an apothecary

neighbours.name: Arboga
neighbours.kind: old market town on the Mälaren
neighbours.distance: about 60 km east-north-east by country road
offers: Old market town with a long history of trade in iron
Hjälmare Canal to Lake Hjälmaren and Mälaren steamers in the open season, May to October
Notaries and carriers for the road west

neighbours.name: Katrineholm
neighbours.kind: railway junction on the trunk line
neighbours.distance: about 100 km east by the main line, around two hours by train
offers: Junction where the southern and western lines divide
Connections to Stockholm, Östergötland and Småland

authorities.police: The kronolänsman of the Kärrtorp district sits at Hallsberg, about 12 km away. He is often called to the station, the navvies' barracks and the goods yard. In the town itself there are only a station constable and a night watchman.
authorities.court: The häradsrätt for the Närke plain meets at Örebro, about 35 km north. It sits at fixed sessions through the year, and cases of railway accident, smuggling and theft from goods wagons come before it. Farmers and railway witnesses travel in by the branch line.
authorities.doctor: The provincial doctor for the Närke plain district lives in Örebro, about an hour by train. He can be fetched by telegram and train, and signs the death certificates. The parish clerk and the old women of the farms still do most of the healing.
authorities.post: There is a post office at the station. Mail arrives and leaves with the trains, several times a day, and the post to the outlying farms is carried on by a rural post-carrier.
authorities.telegraph: The state telegraph office is at Kärrtorp Junction Station and open daily. Messages reach Örebro, Stockholm and Uppsala within hours.
authorities.bank: The nearest bank is Örebro Privatbank in Örebro, about 35 km away by train, with a savings bank there too. The merchants of Kärrtorp deal with it by rail and post.
authorities.newspaper: Nerikes Allehanda is printed in Örebro and comes by the morning train. It carries timetables, court news and reports of railway accidents.

routes.name: By rail via Stockholm and the western main line

legs.cost: roughly 1 riksdaler 50 öre in third class
legs.schedule: Several trains daily, morning to evening
legs.notes: Stops at Knivsta, Märsta and Rotebro. Allow time at Stockholm for the change of stations, an hour at best, and by November it is dark by four.

legs.schedule: Daytime and evening trains daily, fewer on Sundays
legs.notes: The trunk line through Södertälje and Gnesta carries both the southern and western lines. Carriages are cold in November, so travellers bring rugs.

legs.schedule: Several trains daily on the western main line, with a connection to Örebro at the junction
legs.notes: The line runs through Närke by way of Hallsberg. The last train in November arrives after dark, and the Railway Hotel will send a boy with a lantern if told in advance.

routes.name: By road via Enköping, Västerås and Arboga

legs.duration: about 12 hours with changes of horses
legs.cost: roughly 6 riksdaler by post-carriage, with the post-boy's tip
legs.schedule: Post-carriage stages along the old road through Enköping, daily with the post
legs.notes: In November the road is mud and ruts, and daylight is short, so most travellers lie over at the Enköping posting inn.

legs.cost: roughly 8 riksdaler for a hired carriage and driver
legs.schedule: By arrangement with the posting inn at Västerås
legs.notes: A slow, flat road past farms and wayside inns. Fog lies in the hollows by the Mälaren.

legs.cost: roughly 10 riksdaler for a carriage and a change of horses
legs.schedule: By arrangement at Arboga, with an overnight stop at the town
legs.notes: The southern road leads over the plain and past the edge of the marsh, with flooded stretches in the autumn. Carts and wagons are in the way close to the station, and the journey takes two days in all.

journey.journeyScene: The train runs out of Stockholm into the dusk, and the lamps in the carriage shake with every joint in the rail. Outside lie flat fields and black woods, and farm lamps are few and far between. As you come nearer Kärrtorp the engine smoke lies low over the marsh. Then the station bell rings out over the sheds and the new wooden houses, and somewhere beyond them the old church bell answers faintly.

publicFacts: The western main line reached Kärrtorp in 1862 and the branch line to Örebro opened in 1866, making it a junction.
The railway hotel by the station is the best in the district and travellers stay there between trains.
The State Railways employ more than a hundred men at Kärrtorp: engine drivers, firemen, switchmen and workshop hands.
The marsh east of the town was partly drained for the railway embankment and floods every autumn.
The old farmers and the railway people sit on opposite sides of the church.
A free church congregation has started meeting in a hall near the station, to the vicar's displeasure.
The town's lending library was founded by the stationmaster and is open on Wednesday and Saturday evenings.
At Martinmas, servants leave their old places and new ones arrive with their chests on the trains.

places.name: Kärrtorp Junction Station
places.ownerRole: the station master of the junction
places.description: The station is a large brick building with a tower clock and a long covered platform, the busiest place for many miles. Trains arrive in clouds of steam and sparks, the bell rings, and porters push trolleys of luggage through the puddles. The telegraph clatters in the office day and night. Coal smoke, wet iron and the smell of paraffin lamps fill the dark afternoon.

places.description: The railway hotel faces the station, a new three-storey building with plaster ornaments and a dining room with white tablecloths. Travellers wait there between trains, reading newspapers by the stove. The smell of coffee, cigars and roasting goose fills the lobby at Martinmas. Through the windows the lamps of the trains pass slowly in the rain.

places.name: Kärrtorp Church
places.description: The old church stands on a slight rise among the farms, a quarter of an hour's walk from the station, its tower visible across the flat fields. The churchyard is muddy and the lime trees drip. Inside, the old box pews are full of farming families, the railway families in the new benches at the back. Damp has stained the plaster around the windows.

places.ownerRole: the vicar of the parish, who lives here and serves the church
places.description: The parsonage is an old red farmhouse beside the church, larger than the farms around it. Sleet blows against its windows. In the yard the glebe farm's hands are threshing. The vicar's study is crowded with visitors at Martinmas, coming to collect their moving certificates.

places.ownerRole: the smith of the Lindqvist family, who gave the smithy its name
places.description: The smithy is on the old road where it crosses the railway, busier than ever with carts, wagons and the railway's small jobs. Two hearths burn and the smith has an apprentice and a striker. The light of the forge spills out onto the wet road. The clang of the hammer is drowned out every time a train passes.

places.description: The lending library occupies two rooms in a new wooden building near the station, warm and lamplit on its open evenings. Railway workers and clerks sit at the long table with newspapers and books. Rain drums on the window. The librarian, a retired schoolmaster, peers over his spectacles at everyone who enters.

places.name: Kärrtorp Gård
places.ownerRole: a freeholder farming family, the oldest in the parish
places.description: The old farm that gave the town its name now stands with railway sidings at the bottom of its fields. The house is a solid two-storey building with old outbuildings, and the family refuses to sell to the railway company. The threshing goes on in the barn and the sound mixes with the trains. Geese are being fattened in a pen for Martinmas.

places.description: A small grey cottage stands at the edge of the marsh where the embankment cuts across it, the trains thundering past within a stone's throw. The ground around it is waterlogged every autumn. A family of railway navvies lives there now, with the cow sold. The windows rattle at every train.
